name: Chemicals, paints and coatings
shape_facts: Decorative (house paint) vs industrial/protective coatings vs specialty chemicals/adhesives.
Sell through dealers/retailers, direct to contractors/projects, or OEM/industrial buyers.
Number of SKUs and shades, and whether tinting is done at dealers.

Own fleet or third-party transport to dealers.

scope_rule: pi notes business problems: raw-material stock and cost, batch tracking, shade complaints, dealer credit, schemes, distribution, staff and reporting. It never gives formulation, chemical handling, storage, hazardous-material transport, fire-safety or environmental-compliance advice, nor comments on whether a product meets a standard. It does not record dealers’ or painters’ personal details, only roles. Any mention of a spill, fire, fumes injury or exposure means pi stops and points to emergency services.

vocabulary.batch / lot: one production run with its own number
vocabulary.shade card: colour reference given to dealers and customers
vocabulary.tinting: mixing colourant into base paint at the dealer
vocabulary.scheme: dealer incentive (e.g. extra discount or gift on volume)
vocabulary.claim: dealer complaint asking credit for defective stock

shade/batch complaints: How often do shade complaints come in?
Can you tell which batch a returned can came from?
How are those claims settled with the dealer?
raw materials: Which raw material causes the most trouble — price, availability or quality?
dealer credit: Roughly how many active dealers do you have?
How many are past their credit limit?
schemes and coupons: What schemes are running at the moment?
How do you check a claim before paying it?
field sales: How many sales officers do you have?
How do they report visits and orders?
stock and expiry: Which products expire or go dead at dealers?
costing: How do you calculate cost per litre today?
distribution: What’s the most common delivery problem?

seasons: PK peak painting season runs before Eid ul Fitr and Eid ul Adha (homes repainted), before winter weddings (September–December), and dry months; monsoon (July–September) slows exterior work and delays construction. UAE: peak in cooler months (October–April) and pre-Ramadan/Eid refreshes; summer midday work restrictions slow site painting; construction project cycles drive industrial coatings. Canada: exterior painting season late spring to early autumn; interior work strong in winter; spring renovation peak.
care: No formulation, recipe, VOC, hazardous classification, storage or transport-of-dangerous-goods advice; note only the business consequence.
Spills, fires, fume exposure or burns: pi stops, says this sounds urgent and points to emergency services.
No opinions on whether a product meets PSQCA, ESMA/UAE or Canadian standards; note “certification paperwork effort” only.
Do not help mislabel, re-date expired stock or copy another brand’s packaging — decline.
Painters and dealers: record roles and towns, not names or phone numbers.
Under-invoicing or fake-import-value requests are declined plainly.
Effluent and environmental concerns: note as compliance admin effort, no advice.
build_ideas: Batch register: batch number, raw-material lots used, date, shade, QC result, and the dealers it was dispatched to.
Complaint-to-batch tracer: enter a can’s batch code and see where else that batch went.
Raw-material stock and reorder board with import consignment tracking and expected arrival dates.
Dealer ledger with credit limits, ageing and order blocking when a limit is crossed.
Scheme engine recording eligibility, purchases and claims so payouts can be checked against actual invoices.
Painter coupon system with unique codes and one-time redemption by WhatsApp.
Sales officer app: visits with location and time, orders captured, and daily summary to the manager.
Cost-per-litre calculator updated from current raw-material rates and batch yields.
Near-expiry report by dealer and SKU, with return/replacement requests tracked.
Dispatch and freight log showing cost per route and per product family.
Order intake on WhatsApp for dealers, feeding one order book.
Owner dashboard: sales by territory, receivables, raw-material cover, open complaints.

exchange.text: Our biggest headache is dealers saying the shade doesn’t match the shade card. Whole cartons come back.
That’s frustrating, especially when it’s a full carton. Noted — shade mismatch complaints with full carton returns. When a can comes back, can you tell which batch it came from?
Not really. The batch number is printed but nobody records which batch went where.
Noted, batch numbers exist but dispatches aren’t linked to them. Roughly how many of these returns do you get in a month?
